children: Drilling Tools International Holdings Inc. (DTI) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 25, 2026.

On November 24, 2026, Drilling Tools International Corporation (the "Company") and its subsidiary Casing Technologies Group Limited ("Buyer") entered into a First Amendment (the "Amendment") to the Share Purchase Agreement, dated as of October 8, 2026 (the "Share Purchase Agreement"), with Saltire Energy Limited and Foxley Energy Limited (together, the "Group"), the sellers party thereto (the "Sellers") and Jack William Loggie, as Seller Representative (the "Seller Representative").

amends Buyer's financing condition to closing so that it may be satisfied by debt and/or equity financing obtained either on terms consistent with the financing heads of terms attached to the Share Purchase Agreement (the "Agreed Financing Terms") or from other sources, on other terms or in another form or structure as Buyer may determine in its reasonable discretion (an "Alternative Financing"), in each case in an amount sufficient to pay the adjusted closing date cash consideration and Buyer's fees and expenses payable at or prior to closing. Buyer must notify the Seller Representative within five business days after determining to pursue an Alternative Financing, and no Alternative Financing may increase the obligations or diminish the rights of the Group or the Sellers;

extends from November 30, 2026 to January 15, 2027 the date on or after which the Seller Representative may deliver a notice initiating a financing discussion period (a "Financing Discussion Notice");

restates the Seller Representative's termination right so that the Seller Representative may terminate the Share Purchase Agreement only if (i) a Financing Discussion Notice has been delivered on or after January 15, 2027, (ii) the related financing discussion period has expired, and (iii) the Seller Representative and Buyer determine, acting reasonably and in good faith, that there is no reasonable prospect of the financing (including any Alternative Financing) being obtained on or prior to the outside date; and

provides that Buyer and the Company may pursue the Agreed Financing Terms and any Alternative Financing concurrently, that neither the failure to consummate nor the abandonment of the senior secured bond issue described in the Agreed Financing Terms will, in and of itself, constitute a breach of the Share Purchase Agreement by Buyer or the Company, and that, as of the date of the Amendment, no Financing Discussion Notice had been delivered and no party had a right to terminate the Share Purchase Agreement.
Except as expressly modified by the Amendment, the Share Purchase Agreement remains in full force and effect.

The foregoing description of the Amendment does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Amendment, which is filed as Exhibit 10.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference.

Forward-Looking Statements. This Current Report on Form 8-K contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act and Section 21E of the Exchange Act. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including the risks described in Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors" of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC on March 6, 2026 and subsequent filings with the SEC. The forward-looking statements are expressly qualified by the safe-harbor provisions of Section 27A of the Securities Act and Section 21E of the Exchange Act. The Company undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement except as required by law.

No Offer or Solicitation. This Current Report on Form 8-K is not an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities, nor is it a solicitation of a proxy, in any jurisdiction where the offer or solicitation is unlawful. No offering of securities will be made except by means of a prospectus meeting the requirements of Section 10 of the Securities Act or pursuant to an applicable exemption.

Additional Information and Where to Find It. In connection with the proposed issuance of shares in the Transaction, the Company has filed a registration statement on Form S-4 with the SEC that includes a proxy statement/prospectus. INVESTORS AND SECURITY HOLDERS ARE URGED TO READ THE FORM S-4, THE PROXY STATEMENT/PROSPECTUS AND ANY OTHER RELEVANT DOCUMENTS FILED WITH THE SEC

CAREFULLY. Copies of these documents may be obtained free of charge through the SEC's website at www.sec.gov and the Company's website at investors.drillingtools.com, or by contacting the Company at 10370 Richmond Avenue, Suite 1000, Houston, Texas 77042, Attention: Investor Relations.

Participants in the Solicitation. The Company and its directors and executive officers may be deemed participants in the solicitation of proxies from the Company's stockholders in connection with the Transaction. Information about the Company's directors and executive officers, including their direct and indirect interests and beneficial ownership of Common Stock, is set forth in the Company's registration statement on Form S-4, which includes a proxy statement/prospectus, filed in connection with the Transaction and in other filings with the SEC. Additional information regarding interests in the Transaction is included in the Form S-4 and proxy statement/prospectus, which have been filed with the SEC. The solicitation is subject to Rule 14a-12 and the disclosure requirements of Schedule 14A, including Items 4 and 5.
The full text of this SEC filing can be retrieved at: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1884516/000119312526478633/d161991d8k.htm
Any exhibits and associated documents for this SEC filing can be retrieved at: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1884516/000119312526478633/0001193125-26-478633-index.htm
Public companies must file a Form 8-K, or current report, with the SEC generally within four days of any event that could materially affect a company's financial position or the value of its shares.
